claims.text: Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes degradation and premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
A roughly 10–50 nm Al2O3 layer can be deposited by ALD between the zirconium-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating.
The Al2O3 interlayer will inhibit high-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion with the interlayer will prevent premature coating failure.
The barrier-modified coating will retain protective oxidation performance during normal subcritical-water operation.
The barrier-modified coating will retain protective oxidation performance during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
Normal PWR subcritical-water operation is represented by approximately 320°C high-pressure water.
Loss-of-coolant-accident steam exposure can exceed 1000°C for short durations.
The deposited Al2O3 interlayer will remain intact and dense during the specified exposures.
An intact Al2O3 interlayer will physically separate the Cr coating from the Zr-alloy substrate.
The Al2O3 interlayer will preserve the original microstructures of both the Cr coating and the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Al2O3 has a high melting point relevant to its proposed thermal stability.
Al2O3 has low diffusivity for both Cr and Zr under the proposed exposure conditions.
Retarding Cr and Zr transport will reduce deleterious interfacial phase formation.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated control, the barrier-modified system will show significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The intervention is expected to be effective in both the specified PWR-water and accident-steam environments.
Long-term thermal-cycling stability, mechanical adhesion, and interlayer integrity under extreme transients remain uncertain.
